newsitem.title: USA: Silver tureen sells for record $10.3 million.
newsitem.headline: Silver tureen sells for record $10.3 million.

text.p: The value of French Royal Silver went through the roof on Wednesday when a Louis XV tureen sold for a record $10.3 million at a Sotheby's auction.
The collection of French Royal Silver owned by George Ortiz brought a landmark total of $15.3 million, nearly twice the highest previous total for a sale of silver at auction.

The top lot, made in 1733 by Thomas Germain and considered to be the most magnificent piece of silver in private hands, was purchased by an anonymous private bidder over the phone with Ian Irving, Senior Vice President in Sotheby's Silver Department in New York.

The underbidder, London dealers S. J. Phillips, went on to buy the second-highest lot of the sale, a pair of Louis XV Royal Silver wine coolers made by Claude Ballin II. Phillips paid $3.96 million for the lot.

An anonymous bidder purchased a pair of George II Silver three-light candelabra for $816,500. A pair of Louis XV Royal Silver tureen stands went for $123,500 to another anonymous bidder. A pair of Louis XV Silver second course dishes went for $79,500, and a pair of Louis XV Silver jattes, or basins, brought in $57,500.
